text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-007","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"material","page":1,"quote":"Polyurethene"},{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"HARDENED 40-45 HRC"}],"comment":"The title block specifies material as \"Polyurethene\" but also calls for \"HARDENED 40-45 HRC\"; polyurethane is a polymer that cannot be heat-treated to a Rockwell C hardness, creating an impossible manufacturing instruction. The designer must correct either the material or remove the hardness/heat-treatment requirement.","recommended_correction":"Remove the heat treatment and HRC hardness from the title block if the part is polyurethane, or change the material field to a hardenable metal if the hardness requirement is correct."},{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"HARDENED 40-45 HRC"}],"comment":"The drawing specifies a hardness of 40-45 HRC but does not state at which stage of manufacture the heat treatment applies (e.g., before or after machining), which is essential for process planning. The designer should add the required stage to the heat treatment callout.","recommended_correction":"Update the heat treatment note to specify the stage, for example \"HARDEN 40-45 HRC AFTER MACHINING\" or \"HARDEN 40-45 HRC BEFORE FINAL MACHINING\"."}]}
